name: Skeleton from motion
markdown:
# Skeleton from motion

> From the author's earlier studio, cleaned for publication: private paths, ports and some lines were removed, so a step may read short and a screen it names may not exist here. Status in this studio: Tested on the author's old stack.


Status (2026-10-17): **code and tests done (CPU); nothing renders it on the GPU yet.** Code: the earlier studio's skeleton_from_motion.py; tests `tests/studio/test_skeleton_from_motion.py` (fake BVH / NPZ fixtures, plus two checks against the real 2026-10-11 Kimodo and GEM-X clips).

## What it is
The pose-set "pose control" route (`img:klein_posectl`, [pose-set.md](pose-set.md), `the author's research notes` section 7) feeds Klein 9B + the RefControl pose LoRA two pictures: image 1 = an OpenPose / DWPose skeleton, image 2 = the reference. `studio/pose_skeleton.py` DRAWS that skeleton from a hand-made table of 97 bank poses (a small IK body, 18 keypoints, CPU). A motion clip already holds a real skeleton, so this module turns one frame (or a sequence) of it into the same picture with the same `draw`, colours and BODY_18 order:

| Function | Gives | For |
|---|---|---|
| `load_motion(path)` | a `Motion` (joints in metres, Y up) from a `.bvh` (forward kinematics from the file) or a `.npz` (`posed_joints` Kimodo, `joints` GEM-X, or SMPL joints) | all of them |
| `keypoints18(motion, t, yaw)` | the 18 OpenPose points in 3D | checks, other renderers |
| `skeleton_image` / `render_file(motion, t, path, src_size=, frame=, info=)` | the skeleton PNG of one frame, placed on the source's face box like `pose_skeleton.render_file` (same return shape) | **the pose-control route** |
| `render_pose_file("motion:<file>@<frame>", path, ...)` | `pose_skeleton.render_file`'s twin for a motion pose id | the pose-control seam below |
| `render_sequence` / `render_control_video` | a PNG per output frame / an H.264 control video (81 frames at 16 fps by default), anchored on frame 0 so root travel stays travel | **Wan 2.2 Fun Control** (`vset_control_tools.funcontrol_generate(control="pose")` takes a control video) |
| `to_vset_person(motion, t)` | `{"slots", "forward"}` in Blender Z-up for `vset/passes.keypoints3d` | **Virtual Set passes** |

## The joint maps (deterministic)

Measured on the real clips (CPU, 2026-10-17): the module's forward kinematics equals the NPZ joints the same tools wrote (Kimodo `posed_joints` to 0.14 mm, GEM-X `joints` to 1e-7 m), and the skeleton pictures of frames of both clips were rendered and looked at (a standing figure with the arms where the clip puts them, hands drawn).

## Honest limits
Orthographic projection of the 3D joints; the hands are pose_skeleton's simple open-ish hands, not tracked fingers; the RefControl LoRA was trained on DWPose maps, so how well it reads any drawn or derived skeleton is **unproven** (proof level recipe; `scripts/pose_set_proof.py` arm D is the test, and the 3D batch's M4 steps produce motion skeletons to look at); a clip of someone walking away is shown walking toward the camera unless `yaw` says otherwise; SMPL needs joints (an NPZ of parameters only is refused with the reason).

## Seams (nothing below is built; the exact places, so a later change is small)
**Pose-control route.** Two edits in the earlier studio's pose_set.py plus the picker:
1. `Planner.plan` (the `given` poses loop, ~line 951-975): a pose the caller names is a bank id or typed text; an unknown text becomes `{"id": "custom", ...}` and `eng.kind == "posectl"` then refuses any id not in `_skeleton_ids()`. A motion pose needs `{"id": "motion:<file>@<n>", "text": "...", "motion": "<file>", "frame": n}` carried through the picture record, accepted by that check via `skeleton_from_motion.parse_motion_pose_id`.
2. `Run._skeleton` (~line 1165-1185) calls `pose_skeleton.render_file(pic.pose_id, ...)`: dispatch to `skeleton_from_motion.render_pose_file(pic.pose_id, ...)` when `parse_motion_pose_id(pic.pose_id)` is not None (same arguments, same return shape, `mirror` supported).
3. UI: a motion picker in the 10-poses dialog (a finished Kimodo / GEM-X / SAM 3D Body job and a frame slider). Not trivial (selection, hiding, anatomy checks assume bank poses), so it was not wired.

**Wan 2.2 Fun Control.** `render_control_video(motion, out.mp4, (480, 832))` then `vset_control_tools.funcontrol_generate(image=<character sheet shot>, control_video=out.mp4, prompt=..., control="pose")` (81 frames, 16 fps, 9:16 tested; 70 GiB peak, never run on a motion skeleton). The studio entry that would expose it is `vset:funcontrol` (Virtual Set mode A takes the pass from Blender instead). SCAIL-2 (`motion:scail2`, [3d-motion.md](3d-motion.md)) already takes a driver CLIP, which is the existing controlled-body-movement route for a character still.

**Virtual Set passes.** `vset/passes.keypoints3d(person)` reads `person["slots"]` / `["forward"]` from the rig's bones; `to_vset_person` builds that dict from a motion frame (Y-up to Z-up). In the shot runner the action clip of a World Kit character is retargeted onto its rig and Blender renders the bones, so a motion clip already reaches the pose pass through the clip; use `to_vset_person` only to draw a pose pass for a motion with no rig.

**Deliverables / Content Studio shot kinds that need controlled body movement.** Shot kinds are `talk`, `act`, `broll`, `product` (`deliverables.ENTRY`: `h3:cinematic`, `h3:t2va`, `h3:product`; Wan runs map `talk/act/product` to `wan:i2v` and `broll` to `wan:t2v` in `wan_deliverables.py`). H3 and plain Wan I2V take no body-motion input. A motion clip would attach at one point: the shot-rendering step of `deliverables.py` that picks the entry for `s["kind"]` (`talk`/`act`, ~line 1013-1041 where the model and look are chosen). An `act` shot carrying `{"motion": <Kimodo/GEM-X job>}` would go to a controlled route instead of `h3:cinematic`: (a) `motion:scail2` (character still + driver clip: needs the motion rendered as a driver video; SCAIL takes a SAM 3D Body mesh render of a clip), or (b) Wan Fun Control with `render_control_video`. The Content Studio's `poseset` kind (`content_plan.KINDS`) is the one that already reaches the pose-control route; adding `motion` there is the pose-set seam above. No UI was built; both need the author to say which route (SCAIL-2 or Fun Control) judged better first, which is what the 3D batch's G5 / G7 produce evidence for.
